summary: A bank supplying savings and payment accounts, loans, cards and business banking, with digital access through iMobile and other channels.
description: ICICI Bank connects people who need secure payment and saving facilities with households and businesses that need finance. It assesses borrowers, funds loans and investments, runs payment systems and collects repayments. These activities create interest income, fees, funding costs and credit risk.
money: The bank earns interest on loans and investments and fees from relevant banking services. It pays for deposits and other funding, staff, technology and expected credit losses. Deposit balances are money owed to customers, not sales income.
customers: Households, salaried customers, businesses, corporate clients and overseas Indians use different combinations of accounts, finance and payment services.
drivers: Deposit availability and cost, loan pricing, credit quality, fees, operating efficiency, liquidity and regulatory capital.

groups.title: Accounts, deposits and payments
groups.examples: Savings and current accounts, fixed and recurring deposits, debit cards, transfers and iMobile access.
groups.explanation: These help customers store and move money. Deposits also fund the bank, but must remain repayable under their terms.

groups.title: Household borrowing
groups.examples: Home, vehicle, personal and education loans, secured lending and credit cards.
groups.explanation: Different borrowers, collateral and repayment terms create different interest income and loss risks.

groups.title: Business and corporate banking
groups.examples: Working-capital finance, business loans, trade finance, cash management and foreign-exchange services.
groups.explanation: A business can need short-term stock funding, payment collection or longer-term investment finance; these are different credit decisions.

groups.title: Investments and wider financial services
groups.examples: Investment distribution, wealth services and relevant group financial businesses.
groups.explanation: Distributing a product, lending money and owning a financial subsidiary are different activities. Read the entity and fee arrangement.

basics.title: A deposit is a funding obligation; a loan is an asset with risk
basics.text: A customer depositing money creates a liability for the bank. A loan creates an asset expected to generate interest and repayments. The bank must manage the timing of both: a long-duration loan cannot always be converted into cash as quickly as customers may withdraw deposits.

basics.title: Recognise losses before confusing them with recovery
basics.text: A provision is an accounting allowance or charge for expected losses on credit. A write-off changes the accounting treatment and is different from a borrower repaying. Capital buffers absorb losses; liquidity measures help assess whether payments can be met on time. Read all three rather than treating one strong ratio as a complete assessment.

steps.title: Attract and retain funding
steps.text: Build deposit relationships and arrange other eligible funding at an appropriate cost.

steps.title: Assess borrowers and price risk
steps.text: Check ability to repay, collateral and concentration before agreeing loan terms.

steps.title: Service accounts and collect money
steps.text: Operate payment channels, monitor loans and collect interest and principal.

steps.title: Recognise losses and maintain buffers
steps.text: Provide for expected losses while keeping the liquidity and capital needed to operate.

specifics.title: Interest income is not the interest spread
specifics.text: Net interest income subtracts interest expense from interest earned. Net interest margin relates that net income to the stated earning-asset base. It still comes before several other costs and is not the net profit margin of an ordinary retailer.

specifics.title: A growing loan book can hide later losses
specifics.text: Credit problems often emerge after lending. A non-performing asset is a loan classified as impaired under the applicable rules. Slippages describe fresh deterioration; provisions recognise expected losses. Loan growth should be read with all three.

specifics.title: Digital use and financial returns are different
specifics.text: More app users or transactions can improve engagement and lower some servicing costs, but may also need technology investment and controls. Payment volume is not automatically fee revenue or profit.

watch: Are deposits growing on sustainable terms?
Funding must support lending without excessive cost or liquidity pressure.
Compare deposit growth, funding cost and the current/savings account mix with loan growth and liquidity disclosures. A change in mix can matter even when the deposit total rises.
Is lending growth accompanied by sound repayments?
New lending has to remain collectible.
Read gross and net impaired loans, fresh slippages, recoveries, write-offs and provisions together. A write-off can reduce a reported problem-loan stock without meaning the borrower repaid.
What is moving net interest income?
Loan and deposit rates can reset at different times.
Use the stated net interest margin basis, funding-cost discussion and asset mix. Compare matched periods rather than reading a policy-rate change as an immediate equal change in all bank rates.
Do fees and digital relationships cover their costs?
Transaction activity is not the same as earnings.
Read fee categories, operating expenses and technology spending alongside customer activity. Identify recurring banking fees separately from trading or one-off gains.
Are capital and liquidity adequate for the growth?
Accounting profit alone does not fund unlimited lending.
Check regulatory capital, liquidity measures, concentration and standalone versus consolidated scope. Inspect group-company contributions separately from the bank’s own lending results.
risks: Unsecured lending, business stress or concentrated exposures can increase losses and provisions.
Competition for deposits and withdrawal needs can raise funding costs or limit lending flexibility.
Fraud, cyber incidents, outages or compliance problems can create losses and damage trust.
Rate changes affect margins and investment values; the timing and balance-sheet mix determine the impact.
context: Read a recovery differently from a write-off

A recovery brings money back from a stressed borrower. A write-off changes the accounting treatment of a loan; collection may continue afterward. The distinction helps explain why an improving problem-loan ratio should be checked against cash recoveries and fresh deterioration.
quiz: Does a larger deposit balance mean the bank earned more revenue?
No. A deposit is an obligation to the customer and a source of funding. Earnings depend on how funding is deployed, interest and fees earned, funding and operating costs, and credit losses.
sources: FY 2025–26 annual report filed with the SEC

financialNotes.title: Use bank measures on a consistent basis
financialNotes.text: The audited figures cover the consolidated group, including insurance businesses. Gross total income, net interest income and profit after tax measure different stages of the business. Deposits, advances and assets are balance-sheet amounts. The table does not allocate profit to each card, account or loan product.
